name: Pixel Jitter
description: Measures sub-pixel spatial displacement noise between frames to detect the micro-tremor artifacts left by video generation models that process frames without global motion stabilization.
mechanism:
This method detects pixel-level temporal jitter for video deepfake detection:

1. **Sub-Pixel Motion Analysis**: Per-pixel temporal variation is measured in regions that should be static (stationary background, stable facial features during stillness). Sub-pixel motion is extracted using phase-based methods to detect motion below one-pixel magnitude.

2. **Jitter Frequency Analysis**: The temporal frequency content of per-pixel variation is analyzed. Natural video shows specific jitter signatures: (a) sensor read noise (white noise, typically < 1 LSB), (b) quantization dither, (c) compression artifact variation. AI-generated video may show jitter with different spectral characteristics — frame-independent rendering produces temporally uncorrelated pixel variations.

3. **Spatial Jitter Pattern**: The spatial distribution of jitter intensity is mapped. Natural jitter is spatially uniform (same sensor for all pixels). AI-generated jitter may be spatially non-uniform — varying in intensity across the frame or showing different jitter characteristics in generated face regions vs. original background.

4. **Face-Background Jitter Comparison**: Jitter characteristics of face pixels are compared with background pixels. In authentic video, both originate from the same sensor and show identical noise characteristics. Deepfake composites show different jitter signatures between the generated face and original background.

5. **Jitter-Motion Decoupling**: The method separates true motion from jitter to avoid false positives. Genuine micro-motion (physiological tremor, breathing) is distinguished from generation artifacts based on spatial coherence and frequency characteristics. The forensic score quantifies the anomalous jitter component.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through pixel jitter analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
